chunks: Abu Talib al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn al-Muzaffar al-'Alawi al-Samarqandi (RA) said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated from his father Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-'Ayyashi, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Ishkib said: Harun ibn 'Uqbah al-Khuza'i reported to me, on the authority of Asad ibn Sa'id al-Nakha'i, who said: 'Amr ibn Shimr reported to me, on the authority of Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (AS) said:

O Jabir! How great is the slander of the people of Syria against Allah, the Mighty and Exalted. They claim that when Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, ascended to the heaven, He placed His foot on the stone of Jerusalem. And indeed, a servant from among the servants of Allah placed his foot on his stone; hence, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, commanded us to take it as a place of prayer. O Jabir! Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has no rival and no likeness. He is exalted from the attribute of the attributers, and glorified above the imaginations of the imaginers. He is veiled from the eyes of the beholders; He does not decline with the decliners, nor does He set with the transitory. There is nothing whatsoever like unto Him; He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الشَّام: The people of Syria, often used in Shia hadith to denote early anthropomorphists (Mujassima)
key_terms.الوَاصِفِينَ: The attributers (those who attribute physical qualities to God)
key_terms.صَخْرَةِ بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِس: The Stone of Jerusalem (Dome of the Rock)
key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing like unto Him (Quranic verse)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on Allah's physical attributes and the 'foot of God' in the Dome of the Rock?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the Ghulat (exaggerators) in Syria who attributed physical ascent and bodily parts to Allah, a view Imam al-Baqir (AS) corrects by distinguishing divine transcendence from the physical act of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) or other servants. The Imam emphasizes that the 'foot on the stone' refers to a created servant, not God, thereby negating space (makkan) and motion (harakan) for the Divine. The summary concludes with the Quranic principle of *tanzih* (exaltation), affirming that Allah is hidden from human perception and unlike any creation.
